# Spread Love & Acceptance (The Objective Ledger)

> Spread Love & Acceptance is a young, independent start-up building The Objective Ledger: a free, growing suite of self-help tools for understanding yourself and sharing life kindly with the people around you. It brings together practical relationship tools, gentle games, calm breathing and sound spaces, and a plain-language library, with new tools and content added all the time. Everything you type stays on your device.

Key facts:
- Website: https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/ . Free to use; everything opens with a free email sign-up, and much of it needs nothing at all.
- Who it is for: anyone who wants to understand themselves and get along more kindly and fairly with others: partners, families, co-parents, friends, roommates, coworkers and caregivers, and people exploring on their own.
- Themes: self-help, relationships, love, kindness, appreciation, acceptance, reconciliation and repair, calm, peace, harmony, breathing and quiet moments, connection, fairness and the invisible "mental load", and differences in how people are wired.
- The Five Pillars: see the whole load; fix the setup, not the person; read your state first; tune how you send and receive; notice the quiet incentives.
- Privacy: what people type into the tools stays on their own device.
- It is education and self-reflection, not therapy, diagnosis or treatment.
- Mascots: two pups, Tidbit (black mask) and Sugarfoot (white feet). Chat helper: Professor Puddles.
- Status: a young start-up with a working, growing suite; new tools and content are added continually (see https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/whats-new.html).
- Contact: patrick.christian.andrews@gmail.com

## Start here
- [Home](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/): Free self-help for love and acceptance at home: share the mental load, a fair chore chart, calm ways to stop fighting, a communication quiz and a kids’ cartoon.
- [About Spread Love & Acceptance and Its Creator](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/about.html): Meet Christian, the creator of Spread Love & Acceptance and The Objective Ledger: a career auditing systems, and a free, growing suite of kindness tools.
- [Contents: Every Free Tool, Guide and Chapter](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/contents.html): Everything in the program in three parts: tools for understanding yourself, tools for any two people, and where to start in your kind of relationship.
- [The Five Pillars of Fair, Kind Relationships](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/five-pillars.html): Five simple ideas for fair, kind relationships: see the whole mental load, fix the setup instead of the person, read your stress first, and tune how you talk.
- [Glossary: The Words, in Plain English](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/glossary.html): Every word this site uses, from battery to talk window, in one plain sentence with an example, plus each tool’s everyday name beside its technical one.
- [How It Works: An Outside Look at Yourself](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/how-it-works.html): How the program works: a calm, outside view of your life situation, your wiring and what you notice, like an honest auditor with no verdict on your worth.
- [Is This Right for You? What It Is and Isn’t](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/is-this-for-you.html): A free self-help program for your own stress and reactions, and a fair way for two people to see what each carries at home. Education, not counseling.
- [Membership](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/membership.html): Everything on spreadloveandacceptance.com is free with an email sign-up while the program is being built. Paid membership is coming later.
- [Which part of the program to use](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/program.html): The program in one place: six gentle weeks, the Workpaper Suite, the package and report, the fill-in worksheets and the indexes, and which one to use when.
- [Relationship Tools for Couples, Families and Roommates](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/relationships.html): Free ways to share chores fairly, use kinder words and hold calmer check-ins, for couples, families, co-parents, friends, roommates, coworkers and caregivers.
- [Your Self-Discovery Path, Step by Step](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/self-path.html): The self-discovery path: understand your own load, rhythms and reactions first, with a few short worksheets and free tools you can use on your own.
- [Sent this by someone?](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/sent-this.html): Someone sent you Spread Love & Acceptance? Here is what they can and can’t see, what stays yours, and kind ways to say yes, not yet or no.
- [Start Here: Fair Chores, Calm Talks, Kinder Relationships](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/start-here.html): New here? The one idea behind it all, the best free first tools, and a gentle six-week path to fairer chores, fewer fights and kinder talks at home.
- [Start in 10 minutes](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/start-in-10-minutes.html): One short, straight path through the whole idea: check your weather, read the Preface, try one practice card, and log one thing you did today.
- [Ways In: Free While It’s Being Built](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/ways-in.html): Everything here is free while it is being built. Most pages need nothing at all, a free email sign-up opens the rest, and paid membership comes later.
- [What’s new](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/whats-new.html): Everything newly added to the site, and everything that’s grown: new pages, new games, new sounds, and parts of the program that go deeper than before.

## Guides to common questions
- [Fair Chore Chart for Couples (Free, Printable)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/chore-chart-for-couples.html): A free, printable chore chart for couples, families and roommates: list every job, including the invisible ones, give each one an owner and review it weekly.
- [Communication Style Quiz: Find Your Wave Code (Free)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/communication-style-quiz.html): A free communication style quiz: find your four-letter Wave Code and which of 16 archetypes fits, from pace and detail to how you send and receive words.
- [Complacency in Relationships](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/complacency.html): Complacency isn’t laziness. It’s what happens when something has worked for a long time and we stop looking.
- [For Grandparents: Help Without Taking Over](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/grandparents.html): Free, gentle help for grandparents: share childcare fairly, agree on house rules with your adult children, say no kindly, and stay close to your grandkids.
- [How to Stop Fighting With Your Partner: 7 Calm Steps](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/how-to-stop-fighting-with-your-partner.html): Practical, calm ways to stop fighting with your partner: notice the early signs, take a real pause, check your words, and fix the setup behind repeat fights.
- [Invisible Labor and the Mental Load: How to Share It](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/invisible-labor-mental-load.html): What invisible labor and the mental load are, real examples from everyday home life, and five calm steps couples and families can use to share it fairly.
- [Neurodivergent Relationships: ADHD and Autistic Couples](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/neurodivergent-relationships.html): Practical tips for ADHD, autistic and AuDHD couples and families: communication differences, sensory overload at home, plans, chores and kind feedback.

## Tools for kinder conversations and fair relationships
- [Free Relationship Help Chat: Ask Professor Puddles](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/ask.html): Describe what is going on in a relationship and get kind, practical next steps and words you could use. Free and private: what you type stays on your device.
- [Carrier Wave Decoder: When a Talk Starts to Go Wrong](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/carrier-wave-decoder.html): A guided, step-by-step tool for the moment a conversation starts going sideways: check your state, get back in tune, and look back on the week together.
- [Relationship Check-Ins: A Kind Weekly Ritual for Couples](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/check-ins.html): A short, kind weekly relationship check-in for couples, families and housemates: what went well, what felt heavy, and one small change to try next week.
- [Text Thread Reader: Calm Replies After a Fight](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/conversation-reader.html): Paste a text thread after a fight and see where it turned, what each of you may be hearing, and calmer replies built from your own words. Free and private.
- [The Full Path Package and Report](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/full-path.html): One fillable PDF with every workpaper for your road, and a detailed report written from your answers: findings, things worth a second look, recommendations.
- [Know Your Own Wiring: A Self-Discovery Guide](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/know-yourself.html): Why you react the way you do: what is your wiring, what life taught you and what is just today, plus kind words to explain what helps to the people around you.
- [Who Did What This Week? A Free Chore Tracker](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/lemonade-stand.html): A free chore and mental load tracker for one person or a whole home: log who did what this week, see the split or your own load, and talk without blame.
- [Daily Mood Check-In and Stress Check: Today’s Weather](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/quick-checks.html): A one-minute daily mood check-in and stress check: how you are doing today, a gentle forecast for hard talks, and a calm pause with something soothing to do.
- [Tone Checker for Texts: See How Your Message Lands](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/signal-translator.html): A free tone checker for texts: type a message, see how it may land and what they may hear, then get a kinder, clearer way to say it. Private, on your device.
- [A 2-Minute Snapshot of How Your Household Shares the Load](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/snapshot/): A gentle two-minute look at how the shared load is set up at home and how it bends, for couples, families, roommates and teams. Not a test or a diagnosis.
- [The 2-minute snapshot](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/snapshot/snapshot-diagnostic-snapshot-interactive.html): Seven quick questions about how a shared load is set up and how it bends under pressure. You get one of four areas, the scoring shown openly, and one small.
- [Turning Toward: 7 Small Habits for Closer Relationships](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/turning-toward.html): Connection grows in small moments. Seven simple habits for love and appreciation: notice when someone reaches for you, give specific thanks, and repair gently.
- [Wired Differently: Neurodiversity and Communication](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/wired-differently.html): How ADHD, autistic and other differently wired minds can hear the same words differently, and simple ways to share plans, chores and feedback that land.
- [Wiring Card: A One-Page “How I Communicate” Card](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/wiring-card.html): Make a free one-page card about how you take in words, what your silence means, what to avoid and how a request lands best, to share with people you love.

## Worksheets (the Workpaper Suite)
- [Try the workpapers](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/do/): A practice space to try the core worksheets on a worked example before you use your own week. Nothing is saved.
- [Workpaper Playground](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/do/workpaper-playground.html): Practice the core worksheets on a worked example: log a week (WP-01), check a battery (WP-02), name owners (WP-03) and see if the load can last (CALC-01).
- [A Six-Week Guided Program for Fairer Chores](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/prog-01.html): Six gentle weeks, one worksheet a week: see the mental load, give every chore an owner, check your stress and how you talk, then look at what has changed.
- [Program Overview](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/program-overview.html): How the program fits together: the chapters explain the ideas and the worksheets put them to use. It also says plainly what is built today and what is not yet.
- [Suite Index](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/suite-index.html): The official list of what’s built today. If something is listed here, it’s live and ready to use. If it isn’t listed, it isn’t live yet.
- [Is the Chore Split Fair? A Free Calculator (CALC-01)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/workpapers/calculators/calc01-solvency.html): Type in the totals from your chore worksheets, for 2 to 8 people, and see in plain words whether the way you share the household load is working for everyone.
- [Your progress, week by week (REPORT-01)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/workpapers/report-01.html): One place to type in what your worksheets produced each week, and a report that reads them side by side to show where they agree and where they don’t.
- [Who Did What: A One-Week Chore Log and Kind Ways to Say No](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/workpapers/wp-01.html): A one-week log of who did what at home, plus three calm ways to say no or “not right now” without starting a fight. A free worksheet for couples and roommates.
- [Stress Check: How Much Are You Carrying? (WP-02)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/workpapers/wp-02-battery-stress-meter.html): A five-question stress check that separates how much you are already carrying from how upset you are about one thing. A reflection tool, not a test.
- [One Owner per Chore: A Free Household Chore Agreement](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/workpapers/wp-03-raci-treaty.html): Give every recurring household chore one clear owner from start to finish, so nothing slips, nobody nags and you stop re-deciding who does what each week.
- [Mental Load Audit: Find the Chores That Keep Slipping](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/workpapers/wp-04-deficit-audit.html): Once a month, look back at four weeks of chore logs together, find the jobs and arguments that keep coming back, and fix the setup instead of blaming a person.
- [Say It So It Lands: Kinder Words Before You Reply](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/workpapers/wp-09-tone-filter.html): A quick self-check before you answer something that landed hard, so what you say next is calm, clear and something the other person can actually hear.
- [90-Second Daily Check-In for Couples and Housemates](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/workpapers/wp-13-pll-protocol.html): A 90-second daily check-in: one sentence each about how you are doing and what is coming up, so small things do not pile up into a weekend argument. Free.
- [Calm-Down Sounds: Brown Noise, a Low Hum and More](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/wp-11-sound-toolkit.html): Three simple background sounds to try as part of your calm-down plan: a low hum, a soft flutter and brown noise. Free in your browser, and a matter of taste.
- [Calm-Down Kit: A Plan for Heated Moments (WP-11)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/wp-11.html): Make a simple calm-down plan before you need it: your early signs, a pause signal, what helps you settle, and how to come back to the talk kindly and on time.

## Calm, breathing and sound
- [Drift: Calm Visuals and Soft Tones to Unwind](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/calm-visualizer.html): Tell Drift how you feel, put on headphones, and let slow, dreamy visuals, kind words and gentle tones keep you company for a few quiet minutes of calm.
- [Echoes of Gold — The Companion Album](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/echoes-of-gold.html): Echoes of Gold (The Christian Project): the 11-track album that came before The Objective Ledger, produced by Christian, performing as Loves Journey EP.
- [The Night Garden: A Calm Breathing Exercise Game](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/night-garden.html): A breathing exercise you can play: breathe slowly to make flowers bloom, guide fireflies into constellations and stack glowing stones. Free, calm, no timers.
- [Pal Cam TV: A Cozy Cartoon Puppy Cam for Your TV](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/pal-cam-tv.html): Leave two cartoon pups playing and napping on your TV all day, with calm music and light that follows the time of day. Free, no sign-up, ready to cast.
- [Calm Music and Relaxing Soundscapes](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/soundscapes.html): Calm music and relaxing soundscapes: breathing tracks, peaceful ambient pieces and gentle songs about love, acceptance and finding your way back to each other.

## Calm games
- [Daily Crossword Puzzle, Newspaper Style (Free)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/daily-ledger-crossword.html): A free newspaper-style daily crossword with fair, friendly clues, from a quick 5x5 mini to a big Sunday grid. Play in your browser on any device, at your pace.
- [The Frequency Journey](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/frequency-journey.html): Pick Tidbit or Sugarfoot and play a maze chase or a road-and-river crossing. Easy controls, a relaxed pace and no game over, plus the Frequency Buddies cartoon.
- [Calm Games for a Busy Mind: Free, No Timers](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/pause-and-play.html): Free calm games with no timers and no way to lose: the Night Garden breathing game, the Frequency Journey, Word Bloom, crosswords and a cozy word search.
- [The Quest Map](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/quest.html): A friendly map of the whole program, grouped by the Five Pillars. Each chapter, workpaper, guide, tool, game and library shelf lights up as you explore it.
- [Quiet Crossword: Easy, Gentle Mini Crosswords](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/quiet-crossword.html): Small, friendly mini crosswords with gentle clues in five levels from easy to tricky. Free and calm with no timer: a peaceful puzzle for a few quiet minutes.
- [Calm Word Search, No Timer: Quiet Words (Free)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/quiet-words.html): A calm, free word search with soft themes, levels from easy to tricky and no timer. Every word you find leaves a kind thought behind. Play on phone or computer.
- [The Re-check Drive: A Calm Football Game for Keeping…](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/recheck-drive.html): A calm football game with no clock and no way to lose. Do the small, kind things from the complacency playbook for real, and the ball moves toward a field goal.
- [Word Bloom: A Relaxing Letter-Wheel Word Game](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/word-bloom.html): A free, relaxing word game: swipe across a wheel of letters to find the hidden words. Hundreds of levels from easy to tricky, with no timers and no ads.

## The book
- [Why We Get Out of Tune: Communication at Home (Ch. I)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/book/chapter-1.html): Chapter I: why kind people still end up resentful at home, and how small mismatches in pace, tone and what we expect add up, plus how to get back in tune.
- [Is the Chore Split Fair? Division of Labor (Ch. II)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/book/chapter-2.html): Chapter II: a fair way to ask whether the division of labor at home is working for everyone, counting time, effort and the invisible jobs, never blame.
- [Stress and Seeing Things Differently (Chapter III)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/book/chapter-3.html): Chapter III: how a full stress tank changes what we hear and say, why the same moment looks different from each side, and how to pause before you react.
- [Equal vs Fair: Two Kinds of Fair at Home (Ch. IV)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/book/chapter-4.html): Chapter IV: equal and fair are not the same thing. How couples and families find a fair chore split that fits their real lives, strengths and seasons.
- [The Monthly Relationship Look-Back (Chapter V)](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/book/chapter-5.html): Chapter V: a calm monthly look-back for couples and households to see what changed, celebrate it, and adjust the setup before resentment builds up.
- [Invisible Labor at Home: The Work Nobody Sees](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/book/preface.html): The Preface: the planning, remembering and noticing that keeps a home running, why this invisible work goes unseen, and how seeing it changes everything.

## The Professor’s Library and further reading
- [The Frequency Framework: Getting Back in Step](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/frequency-framework.html): Two people can each run on their own rhythm for money, rest, decisions, talking and values. Why kind people fall out of step, and how to find the beat again.
- [Stories From Philosophy for Everyday Life](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/learn/): Twelve old stories from philosophy, retold in plain words, to help you know yourself, see the other person more clearly and live more kindly with others.
- [Relationship Psychology Library, in Plain English](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library.html): Hundreds of plain-language entries on relationships, conflict, kindness, gratitude, emotions, stress, calm and wiring, with honest notes on the evidence.
- [Calm and Attention, Explained](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/calm.html): What research says about calm and attention: breathing, mindfulness, nature, rest, mind-wandering and flow, with modest and honest claims about each one.
- [Communication in Relationships: Talking and Listening](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/communication.html): Plain-language research on communication in relationships: listening, asking, feedback, tone, apology and the everyday skills of being understood.
- [Conflict Resolution in Relationships, Explained](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/conflict.html): Plain-language research on conflict in relationships: why arguments escalate, how repair works, apology, forgiveness, mediation and fair process.
- [Kindness, Gratitude and Connection, Explained](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/connection.html): What research says about kindness, gratitude, appreciation and connection: small daily rituals, thanks that lands and the habits that keep people close.
- [Understanding Feelings and Emotions](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/emotions.html): Plain-language research on feelings and emotions: naming them, shame and guilt, anger, rumination, grief and resilience, with honest notes on the evidence.
- [The Mental Load and Fair Division of Labor at Home](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/fairness.html): What research says about the mental load, invisible work and the division of labor at home, why each person often thinks they do more, and what helps.
- [Family, Money and Big Life Changes](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/life.html): Plain-language research on family life, money talks, co-parents, holidays, in-laws and the big transitions of life, and how to share the load through them.
- [Motivation, Habits and Change, Explained](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/motivation.html): Plain-language research on motivation, habits and change: mindset, self-esteem, values, rewards and the small steps that help a new habit stick for good.
- [How Relationships Work: What Research Says](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/relationships.html): What research on couples, families and friends says about what keeps people close: attachment, trust, appreciation, repair and sharing the load at home.
- [Stress and the Body, in Plain English](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/stress.html): How stress shows up in the body and in relationships, in plain words: the stress response, polyvagal theory and its critics, sleep, hunger and burnout.
- [Fair Systems for Teams and Households](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/teams.html): How fair systems work for teams and households: clear owners, blameless reviews, checklists, and why shared jobs slip when everyone owns them at once.
- [Common Thinking Traps, Explained](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/thinking.html): Plain-language guides to common thinking traps: why we jump to conclusions, expect the worst, remember selectively and misread each other, and what helps.
- [Neurodiversity Explained: Autism, ADHD and Sensitivity](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/library/wiring.html): Plain-language entries on differences in wiring: autism, ADHD, the double empathy problem, high sensitivity, sensory overload, personality and chronotype.
- [Observational Podcast: The Kane and Christian Experience](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/podcast-index.html): The Objective Ledger podcast series: episodes exploring workpapers, chapters, and real-world applications of the framework with Kane and Christian.
- [Further Reading](https://spreadloveandacceptance.com/reading.html): Hand-picked articles from Psychology Today, Greater Good Magazine, The Gottman Institute and other trusted sources, sorted by topic and by the Five Pillars.
